label: Evaluation constrained by access
definition: Independent evaluation conclusions are materially bounded by documented access/time limits for an identified exercise.
rule: All conditions necessary; their conjunction sufficient for the bounded assessment, not for global provider dependence.

label: Contested contractual interface
definition: Documented use and conflicting positions on contractual conditions trigger consequential institutional action.
rule: All conditions necessary and jointly sufficient for a dated contested-interface finding. No dependency conclusion follows.

label: Operational dependence
definition: A specified institutional function relies on a provider-controlled capability and faces materially constrained substitution.
rule: All conditions necessary, jointly sufficient only for the named function, time and horizon. Control may include demonstrated continuing supply/update access, not merely remote shutdown. Contract restrictions alone insufficient. Counterevidence must be resolved.

label: Transitional operational dependence
definition: Reliance on a provider-specific capability in an existing operational function where immediate withdrawal is constrained by maintaining that function during replacement. This permits alternatives and divided technical control.
rule: All five conditions supported, with government operational-continuity evidence and a distinct instrument or deployment record. Announced procurement, continued use alone, or a phase-out deadline alone is insufficient.
revisionRationale: Separate transition-constrained product dependence from dependence on an ongoing service or remote provider control. This distinction applies symmetrically to any supplier, including offline deployed systems; it is not a relaxation of evidence requirements or a claim that all purchases create dependence.
